newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A government delegation may visit the Indian state of Tripura early next month in a fresh bid to persuade some 40,000 tribes people, living in refugee camps, to return home.

Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, the student wing of main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), on Sunday began an indefinite strike at the Dhaka University to protest what it said the "capture" of a student dormitory by ruling Awami League activists.
An appraisal mission of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is now visiting Bangladesh to explore the possibility of financing a $80 million project to develop the country's capital market.
Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) on Sunday appealed to relevent authorities in European Union states not to harrass importers of Bangladeshi apparels under GSP.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria has expressed concern at the decline of external aid and the changing pattern away from food aid and balance of payment support.
The government has agreed to declare the tea sector as an export-oriented industry.
The country's export earnings during the 1996-97 fiscal year (July-June) stood at $4.42 billion, an increase of 13 percent over the previous fiscal year.
The government is likley to initiate a feasibility study on the proposed deep-sea port. REUTER
